items.title: [ft.com] TSMC and Samsung pause China chip shipments under US controls
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (TSMC), the world’s largest contract chipmaker, and South Korea’s Samsung Electronics have paused some chip shipments to Chinese customers while seeking U.S. licenses under controls that took effect Nov. 19. The rules target both advanced-chip exports and access to computing power through overseas data centers, closing routes Chinese companies had used to obtain processors and computing capacity. The rules also remove exemptions previously used for chips described as intended for non-AI purposes. The companies have notified some consumer-electronics customers of shipment suspensions. TSMC makes smartphone chips for Xiaomi, Oppo and Vivo; an industry source said licenses for smartphone chips were likely to be approved but delays could disrupt production. The controls require closer scrutiny of customers, ownership and shipment routes, including orders placed through overseas subsidiaries or intermediaries. Industry executives told Nikkei the licensing requirements are also affecting ordinary mobile and consumer applications and developers outside China.

items.title: [energynews.biz] US regulator approves four advanced reactors for Dow’s Texas plant
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

The U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) approved construction permits on Nov. 9 for four advanced reactors at Dow’s Seadrift chemical complex on the Texas Gulf Coast, a project developed with reactor company X-energy. The units are intended to provide electricity and process heat to the site. The permits do not commit Dow to build or authorize the reactors to operate; Dow expects to consider a preliminary investment decision in 2027, while X-energy forecasts operations in the early 2030s. Regulators and developers point to design features intended to limit accident risks, while Union of Concerned Scientists safety director Edwin Lyman has challenged claims that the fuel is meltdown-proof. The NRC dismissed a local environmental group’s legal challenges to the permit application.

items.title: [theglobeandmail.com] B.C. storm warnings escalate as coast faces 250 mm of rain
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Environment Canada escalated rainfall warnings for southwest British Columbia as a new storm system was forecast to bring more than 250 millimetres of rain to parts of Vancouver Island. Heavy rain was expected Tuesday and Wednesday, with rain continuing later in the week. Orange warnings cover west and central Vancouver Island, Howe Sound and the Sea to Sky; the provincial River Forecast Centre issued a flood watch for much of southwest B.C. The incoming storm follows weekend winds and rain that killed a driver in Surrey. Police also linked the storm to the death of a 78-year-old Vancouver pedestrian, and a canoeist is missing off northern Vancouver Island. Nearly 415,000 BC Hydro customers lost power at some point, and about 13,300 remained without electricity by late Monday afternoon. In Zeballos, evacuation orders and alerts remained in force for properties threatened by landslides. Officials expected to issue another update Friday, Nov. 13.

items.title: [cbc.ca] Alberta bill sets data-centre limits and well cleanup funds
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Alberta introduced Bill 42 on Nov. 18, proposing new siting and water rules for large data centres and mandatory cleanup funding for every new oil and gas well. Centres using at least 10 megawatts would generally have to be at least 600 metres from homes and avoid top-quality or irrigated farmland; they would also face a near-zero cooling-water standard. The Alberta Utilities Commission would regulate the larger facilities. The province says about 30% of current proposals could be affected, while projects already far along in approvals or construction would be exempt. For new wells, companies would pay up to $50,000 initially and make equal annual payments for up to 10 years. The money would remain attached to the well if ownership changes. If a well becomes orphaned, its funding would go to the Orphan Well Association. The requirements are expected to cover wells drilled after April 1, 2027. The bill would also eliminate Alberta’s oil-sands emissions cap, which the province says is redundant with industrial carbon pricing.

items.title: [theguardian.com] European-Japanese BepiColombo prepares to enter Mercury orbit after eight years
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

The European-Japanese BepiColombo mission is due to enter orbit around Mercury on Nov. 21 after an eight-year journey of about 6 billion miles, becoming only the second mission to orbit the planet. Its two orbiters will investigate Mercury’s surface, interior and magnetic environment, including its unusually large metal core, the origins of its magnetic field and ice in permanently shadowed craters. A propulsion-system problem delayed BepiColombo’s arrival, and reaching Mercury requires careful braking against the Sun’s gravity. The European Mercury Planetary Orbiter will map the surface’s composition and study the interior; Japan’s orbiter will measure the magnetic field and the planet’s thin sodium exosphere. The spacecraft are scheduled to separate on Dec. 9–10, with science operations planned to begin in April 2027.

items.title: [thestar.com] McGill report finds deepfake network spreading false Canada-U.S. trade claims
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

A McGill University research centre says a network of nearly 300 TikTok and Instagram accounts has circulated more than 3,201 deepfake videos that drew 22.1 million views over three months. Many focused on Canada’s trade dispute with the United States. One widely viewed false story described a nonexistent 48-hour ultimatum from President Donald Trump and claimed Prime Minister Mark Carney responded by cancelling $8 billion in U.S. defence contracts. It appeared in 161 videos on 129 accounts and drew 5.1 million views. The report says the accounts promote misleading claims from both sides of the trade debate, while the network’s operators and purpose remain unknown. Researchers said posting patterns and some accounts’ Chinese-language settings or registrations in China point to activity outside North America, but they could not firmly attribute the network to anyone. The report says the accounts have not been monetized and could be building an audience for later use, testing a tool or operating on behalf of someone seeking to influence Canadians.

items.title: [news.mit.edu] Older adults show weaker brain-clearing fluid waves during sleep
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

MIT researchers found that older adults had significantly weaker waves of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF), which helps clear waste from the brain during sleep, than younger adults. The researchers used brain imaging and electroencephalography to study volunteers ages 18 to 39 and 60 to 84, linking the reduced flow partly to weaker deep-sleep brain waves and diminished vascular responses. Separately, a study described in a paper shared on Reddit found that LSD-related gene-expression patterns in rats and mice ran counter to some patterns associated with human brain aging. LSD also reduced certain amyloid-beta-related changes in mouse brain-cell cultures. These are preclinical findings, not evidence that LSD prevents dementia in people.

items.title: [doctorsonly.co.il] Three cardiac teams report aortic repair, heart pump and nerve block
items.content_html:
🔧 ✏️

Doctors at Beilinson Hospital repaired a woman’s enlarged aortic arch without opening her chest, using an endovascular device tailored to her. The technique has been used in about 70 cases worldwide. In Warsaw, a hospital implanted its first left ventricular assist device, an artificial pump that supports the heart, and activated a heart-transplant waiting list. Separately, Chinese doctors reported treating a 53-year-old woman who had repeated dangerous arrhythmias after going into cardiac arrest during surgery for a leg fracture. After medication failed to stop the episodes, a left-sided nerve block was followed by a marked reduction in abnormal heart rhythms within about five minutes.
